extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys and practitioners who practice before the USPTO (particularly trademark/non-patent practitioners), law firms, and USPTO enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and disciplinary criteria governing attorneys who practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters, with emphasis on conflicts of interest, supervision, third-party payments, diligence, and sanctions/reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO disciplinary jurisdiction and applicable rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners practicing before the Office in trademark matters are subject to disciplinary jurisdiction under 37 C.F.R. § 11.19; the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112); and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901). The USPTO Director has jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who is covered by the Office's disciplinary regime and which sets of rules apply when evaluating practitioner conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate conflicts-of-interest inquiry / new matter vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner (and staff acting on practitioner's behalf) must perform an adequate conflicts check when opening a new matter and include all relevant clients in the new matter memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of failing this rule: associate included only the third-party payor (Client 5) on the new matter memorandum and omitted the new clients (Client 1 and Client 2); the partner did not review or correct the memorandum. An inadequate conflicts check can give rise to disciplinary violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain informed consent after full disclosure for joint representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Before accepting or continuing joint representation, the practitioner must disclose the risks and benefits of joint representation to each client and obtain informed consent after full disclosure (37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a); § 10.66(a)-(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record cites failure to make disclosures to Client 1 about joint representation and failure to obtain Client 1's informed consent as a violation. Practitioners must explain possible effects on independent professional judgment and the exercise of that judgment for each client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline representation when independent judgment likely affected or interests differ
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must decline proffered employment if the exercise of independent professional judgment would likely be adversely affected or would involve representing differing interests (37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a)-(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuing representation would impair independent judgment or involve differing interests, the practitioner must either decline the matter or secure consent after full disclosure; failure to do so is sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and consent for third-party payment of legal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must obtain consent after full disclosure before accepting compensation from one other than the practitioner’s client or anything of value related to representation (37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1)-(2) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent billed Client 5 for services provided to Client 1 without disclosing the third-party payment or obtaining Client 1's informed consent, which violated the rule. Also prohibits allowing a payer to direct the practitioner's professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect client confidentiality and obtain consent before including third parties in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not include third parties in confidential communications regarding a client's legal matter without informing the client and obtaining the client's informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: copying third-party payors (Client 3 and Client 4) on confidential emails to Clients 1 and 2 without advising or obtaining consent from Client 1 was cited as a failure to disclose and obtain consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to advise and obtain client consent before abandoning client-owned filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must counsel co-owners/clients regarding filing an express abandonment of an application that a client co-owns and must obtain that client's informed consent before taking such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to counsel Client 1 about the planned Express Abandonment and failure to obtain her consent were disciplinary failures; filing an abandonment that harms a co-owner's interests without counsel/consent is sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on third parties directing or regulating the practitioner's professional judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to render legal services for another to direct or regulate the practitioner's professional judgment (37 C.F.R. § 11.504(c); § 10.68(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement cites permitting payors to participate in and influence decisions adverse to a client's interests (e.g., directing abandonment and refiling in another entity) as a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory obligations to ensure subordinate conformity and remediate known misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: As a practitioner with supervisory or managerial authority, one must make reasonable efforts to ensure subordinates conform to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and must avoid or mitigate known conduct when its consequences can be avoided or take reasonable remedial action (37 C.F.R. § 11.501(b) and (c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent, as partner and Client Responsible Partner (CRP), failed to intervene when a subordinate intended to take action adverse to Client 1 and failed to ensure the associate's compliance; supervisory failures form a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of diligence / do not neglect entrusted legal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not neglect legal matters entrusted to them (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stipulated facts cite neglect in failing to recognize that filing a trademark application on behalf of a co-applicant created a client relationship requiring protections; neglect can include failing to advise or protect co-clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors relevant to discipline (remorse, CLE, lack of prior discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining discipline, mitigating circumstances such as expressed contrition, prompt remedial steps, voluntary continuing legal education (CLE) on relevant topics, and absence of prior discipline may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent completed CLE classes on conflicts of interest, expressed remorse, had no prior discipline in 37+ years—these facts were recited as mitigation and influenced the agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning options and specific agreed sanctions for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions may include suspension from practice before the Office in trademark/non-patent matters, probation, mandatory CLE, examination requirements, restrictions on practice, and filing conditions for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case Respondent agreed to a 30-day suspension (commencing 14 days after signing), 18 months' probation, required MPRE with score of 85 within 1 year, required CLE courses, cooperation with OED, and other compliance obligations with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and procedures for notification, compliance, and reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspended practitioners must comply with client notification, cessation of practice during suspension, and specific petition and fee requirements for reinstatement; many procedural provisions may be imposed or waived in an order (see 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60 and § 11.3(a) delegations/waivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specified which subsections of §§ 11.58 and 11.60 Respondent must comply with or which were waived, required filing a petition for reinstatement with required fee and sworn declaration of compliance, and spelled out conditions under which the OED Director may seek additional suspension for probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED enforcement process for probation violations (Order to Show Cause and possible additional suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply during probation, OED will issue an Order to Show Cause, permit a response, and may request the USPTO Director impose an immediate additional suspension of up to 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure includes sending the Order to Show Cause to the respondent's address of record, granting 15 days to respond, and forwarding materials to the USPTO Director if further suspension is sought; remedial process is administrative and can result in further discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and use of disciplinary records
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders may be electronically published in OED's FOIA Reading Room and a materially consistent notice may be published in the Official Gazette; the record may be considered in future proceedings or to rebut representations by the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order required publication of a notice of suspension and probation, and provided that the Office may consider the record in subsequent complaints or proceedings as aggravation or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlements may include waivers of procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may agree, as part of settlement, to waive rights to seek reconsideration, review, appeal, or otherwise challenge a Final Order under certain 37 C.F.R. provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent waived rights to seek reconsideration under § 11.56, review under § 11.57, and otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order as part of the agreement.
